articles.title: “A Case Study In How To Mismanage A Young QB”: Texas Insider Rips Steve Sarkisian Over Arch Manning’s Struggles
articles.summary: The Texas Longhorns have been struggling of late, barely beating Tennessee, losing two straight games, and Arch Manning has struggled to lead the offense in...
articles.body:
The Texas Longhorns have been struggling of late, barely beating Tennessee, losing two straight games, and Arch Manning has struggled to lead the offense in the last few games. As a result, Manning's draft stock has taken a hit, and Texas has gone down from No. 1 to No. 19 in the AP Top 25 in just two weeks.

Now, ESPN's Pete Thamel is reporting that backup quarterback KJ Lacey Jr. has been getting more first-team quarterback reps, though he noted that Arch Manning would likely still be the QB1 but could be replaced if he continues to struggle.

With Texas struggling and Arch Manning not playing as well as expected, many are also pinning the blame on Texas head coach Steve Sarkisian. One of them is insider Graham Coffey, who blasted the Texas head coach in a very long post on social media:

"The entire Arch Manning – Texas marriage will go down as a case study in how to mismanage a young QB. If Sark crashes out this season, the last week will be a microcosm of why Texas keeps squandering super talented rosters," he wrote. "Last week he tells us Arch would be praised if he didn't have a different last name. A few days later he says Arch's job status is up for evaluation. Nobody in college football draws a wider range of headlines than Arch Manning, and his coach consistently pours gasoline on that fire."

This comes after Sarkisian defended Arch Manning after the loss against Florida, before saying that he was evaluating the quarterback's performance and not ruling out benching him. This then led to Lacey getting more first-team reps.

After his performance against then-No. 1 Ohio State during Week 2, Arch Manning became one of the favorites to be the No. 1 pick in the NFL draft. Kalshi had Manning at 31% back then, but after struggling against UTSA and Tennessee and then the two straight losses against Oklahoma and Florida, he has been plummeting steadily, according to Sports Illustrated.

In those two losses, he had a total of 433 passing yards, four passing touchdowns, and two interceptions, but he also got sacked seven times. For now, Ohio State wide receiver Jeremiah Smith remains the favorite as Manning continues to fall.

articles.title: How Many Rotation Spots Should Angels Allocate To Young Pitchers?
articles.summary: The Los Angeles Angels will have resources next year, which makes their rotation especially interesting.
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Angels are about to have resources, which would seem to indicate an abundance of possibilities. Some kind of fast forward is going to happen in their rebuild once the ownership group of Stan Kroenke takes over after the first of the year.

One of those possibilities is about the rotation. It was an Angels' strength during the second half of the season, but it also raises an intriguing question going forward:

How many rotation spots should the Angels allocate to their group of promising young pitchers?

We already know what the top of the rotation looks like. Left-hander Reid Detmers is the ace, with rookie right-hander Walbert Urena right there with him. That means one slot is automatically allocated to a rookie, which is risky given that Urena's development next year may not be linear.

After that things get messy. Ryan Johnson certainly earned a shot at the No. 3 starter spot with a strong second half of the season, but that introduces even more risk going forward given how young Johnson is and how much of a roller coaster his brief career has been to date. Do the Halos really want to slot him in that high in the rotation?

There are veterans available to fill those last couple of spots, but that option is even messier. Yusei Kikuchi was been a reliable innings-eater for the last few years, but this year he was hurt, and Kikuchi has been the definition of mediocrity for most of his recent career. He's due $21 million in 2027. and he could easily be moved.

There's also Grayson Rodriguez, and he represents an even worse choice. He was able to make it back to the mound after an injury-plagued career, but he doesn't belong anywhere near the rotation of a team that wants to contend. The Angels would probably love to move him, but they'd be selling low given that he has absolutely no value right now.

The easy answer is to go get another veteran to go with Reid Detmers. Heck, given Kroenke's deep pockets, go get another ace. The attention would help the Halos compete with the Los Angeles Dodgers, which would be fun to watch and great for both teams.

It doesn't necessarily have to be Tarik Skubal, either. Sonny Gray will be available, and he didn't sound all that thrilled about pitching for the Boston Red Sox again. Other names will be out there and available, and the Angels should go get one of them.

articles.title: NASCAR Cup Stars Returning to JR Motorsports For Select Races in 2027
articles.summary: NASCAR Cup Series drivers Ross Chastain and Shane van Gisbergen will return to JR Motorsports to run select O’Reilly Auto Parts Series races in 2027. The Tra...
articles.body:
NASCAR Cup Series drivers Ross Chastain and Shane van Gisbergen will return to JR Motorsports to run select O'Reilly Auto Parts Series races in 2027. The Trackhouse Racing Cup Series duo will split races in the No. 9 JR Motorsports Chevrolet.Details regarding what races Chastain and van Gisbergen will be behind the wheel for have not been revealed. Chastain, a three-time O'Reilly Auto Parts Series winner, began racing part-time for JR Motorsports in 2025.SVG, a six-time O'Reilly Auto Parts Series winner, also joined JR Motorsports for a part-time slate in 2025. As announced on Tuesday, the two will be back in action for Dale Earnhardt Jr.'s team in 2027.

Ross Chastain, SVG returning to JR Motorsports in 2027

JR Motorsports' social media team broke the news of Chastain and SVG returning to the organization for "multiple" O'Reilly Auto Parts Series races next year."Back in our House and back in the No. 9 for multiple races each in 2027," via JRM on X.Chastain competed in five O'Reilly Auto Parts Series races in both 2025 and 2026 behind the wheel of the No. 9 Chevrolet. He has one victory with the organization, which came in the rain-shortened Charlotte race last May.SVG started in three O'Reilly Auto Parts Series races in 2025 and 2026. The New Zealand native posted a win at the Chicago street course in 2025 and two wins in 2026 at Circuit of The Americas and Sonoma.On the Cup side, 2026 has been a struggle for Chastain. "Melon Man" has gone winless through 33 races and failed to make the Chase for the second time in three seasons.SVG failed to make the Chase, too, as he was the first driver below the cut line at the end of the regular season. The road-course ace earned two wins this season at Watkins Glen and Sonoma.

JR Motorsports Signed Tristan McKee to Developmental Deal

In addition to bringing back two NASCAR Cup Series veterans, JR Motorsports is bringing in youth in 2027. Last Friday, it was announced that Tristan McKee, a 16-year-old developmental driver for Spire Motorsports, will compete part-time for JR Motorsports in 2027.McKee was the 2026 ARCA Menards East Series champion. The youngster out of Williamsburg, Virginia is on the fast track to climbing through NASCAR's top ranks. In a statement by the team, McKee expressed his gratitude for the opportunity with JR Motorsports."I can't wait to get started at Bristol next year with JRM. It means the world to have the opportunity to compete in one of their cars and I can't thank Dale (Earnhardt Jr.), Kelley, LW and everyone at JRM and Spire for this chance. I'm really looking forward to seeing what we can build together," McKee said.McKee will make his O'Reilly Auto Parts Series debut in the No. 9 JR Motorsports Chevrolet in the August 2027 race at Bristol. In addition, McKee will compete part-time for Spire Motorsports in the Craftsman Truck Series.McKee is a four-time winner in the ARCA Menards Series and an eight-time victor in the ARCA East Series. He won three races during the 2026 ARCA East season en route to the championship.

articles.title: How many games can Michigan win the rest of regular season if Tommy Carr is QB1?
articles.summary: Predict how many wins Michigan will have the rest of the regular season if Tommy Carr is the starting quarterback.
articles.body:
Welcome to SB Nation Reacts, a survey of fans across the NCAA. Throughout the year we ask questions of the most plugged-in Michigan fans and fans across the country.

The 4-2 Michigan Wolverines made a change at quarterback at halftime last week. Tommy Carr relieved Bryce Underwood of his duties and put points on the scoreboard. Carr entered the game versus Penn State with Michigan trailing 3-0, and the Wolverines would go on to win the game 21-18. Carr was 5-of-7 for 47 yards with four carries for 36 yards and a touchdown.

Michigan head coach Kyle Whittingham hasn't said who will be Michigan's starting quarterback this Saturday versus Indiana, but also said there's a "secret" plan in place. Carr looked plenty good enough to warrant a start this weekend, and it seems fairly easy to predict he'll be on the field over Underwood on Saturday.

In this edition of SB Nation Reacts, we're asking how many wins Michigan will have the rest of the season if Carr is QB1. Vote below.

Here's a look at Michigan's six remaining matchups and their chances of winning each game, according to ESPN Analytics.

Oct. 24 vs. No. 6 Indiana: 17.8% chance of winning

Oct. 31 at Rutgers: 80.8% chance of winning

Nov. 7 vs. Michigan State: 77.3% chance of winning

Nov. 14 at Oregon: 18.3% chance of winning

Nov. 21 vs. UCLA: 61.7% chance of winning

Nov. 28 at Ohio State: 8.4% chance of winning

ESPN Analytics give Michigan way too low a chance versus Indiana, Oregon, and Ohio State. Oregon QB Dante Moore has been out for weeks, Ohio State quarterback Julian Sayin could be out for the season, and Indiana looks more vulnerable than they did a season ago when they won the national championship. Could Michigan win out and go 10-2? Yes. Could they also lose a few of these? Yes. However, Carr could be the spark Michigan needed to make a run. There seems to be optimism that Michigan can indeed have a strong second half of the season. It'll have to start with a win on Saturday.

How did you vote this week? Let us know in the comments.

articles.title: Kentucky defensive spotlights in road win over Oklahoma
articles.summary: Kentucky's defense showed up on the road against Oklahoma. Here are some players that stood out and made an impact for the Wildcats defense.
articles.body:
Kentucky football moved to 6-1 and are now ranked 12th in the country after defeating Oklahoma on the road. It was impressive to see the Wildcats win a low-scoring defensive game script, which is a style of game that haven't faced all season. I thought Kentucky's defense had their best performance of the season, they were leaky at times in the first half but they really flipped the switch in the second half of this game. Here are a few defensive players that stood out and made an impact on Kentucky leaving Norman with a win.

Ty Bryant continues to find the football and be a ball hawk on the back end. Bryant is a veteran leader of this defense and he always capitalizes on errant throws. His first interception was an assist from Mi'Quise Humphrey-Grace that looked like an arm punt from John Mateer. Bryant then caught the game sealing interception on a deep ball over the middle.

We spoke all offseason on how critical this experienced safety duo would be for Jay Bateman's defense, and Castell has been one of the most consistent transfers on the team this season. Castell is a sure tackler like Ty Bryant and he has ball hawking traits as well. Castell had a pass breakup in the red zone and intercepted the horribly attempted jump pass fake field goal from the Oklahoma punter. The biggest play of the game was Castell's pick six, he read the eyes of Mateer and jumped the pass to take it back to extend the lead late for Kentucky.

Mi'Quise Humphrey-Grace is one of the most consistent players on this defense, he shows up every Saturday and makes big time plays. Against Oklahoma, he got a quick win on the edge and got his hand on Mateer's arm mid-release which set up an easy interception for Ty Bryant. This was a critical play as the Sooners were driving up six points, and this really swung the momentum to Kentucky's favor. Humphrey-Grace batted a ball at the line of scrimmage, he also had 1.5 sacks and 1.5 tackles for loss on Saturday.

Tavion Gadson needs to play with more consistency, but man he is dangerous on the inside when it all comes together. Gadson is one of the most underrated defensive tackles in the country and he has incredible pass rush tools for his size. He was active against Oklahoma and creating negative plays by defeating his blocks quickly against guards. articles.title: Colin Cowherd denounces Junior Caminero’s home run trot: ‘That was obnoxious’
articles.summary: Tampa Bay Rays superstar Junior Caminero is making baseball fun again, but Colin Cowherd is the fun police. Caminero had his moment Monday night, hitting a m...
articles.body:
Tampa Bay Rays superstar Junior Caminero is making baseball fun again, but Colin Cowherd is the fun police.

Caminero had his moment Monday night, hitting a monster seventh-inning home run off Cleveland Guardians closer Cade Smith that all but punched Tampa's ticket to the World Series. The towering blast gave the Rays a 5-1 lead, and they won Game 6 of the ALCS 7-3 to advance to their third World Series in franchise history.

Perhaps more notable than the homer, however, is that Caminero took 38 seconds to round the bases. Caminero stopped several times to pose and pound his chest in celebration because, well, it was the biggest hit of his career.

Baseball purists have waved the white flag on a pitch clock; they've let the DH into the National League; they've even allowed some semblance of celebrating on the field, but Colin Cowherd and others still are not ready to see a player take 38 seconds to trot around the bases.

"I am for celebrating; I think baseball sometimes needs to lighten up," Cowherd admitted. "That is way over the top rounding first. Baseball for years was like, 'There's a way to play the game,' and everybody else had a different idea on the way to play the game. But right before he got to home plate, he stopped, I thought, 'Oh, this is obnoxious.' Two things can be true: I'm all for flexing; that was obnoxious. It's his style. He's a bit over the top, it felt obnoxious to me."

Rip players for celebrating after hitting a solo home run that made the score 8-2 in an elimination game . Mock teams for wearing goggles and popping champagne every time they clinch something . If this happened in the first inning of a June game, Cowherd would have a point. But when a home run essentially sends your team to the World Series, let the player take 38 seconds to flex.

articles.title: Usain Bolt pledged J$10 million with Puma to help restore damaged schools across Jamaica
articles.summary: Last year, when Hurricane Melissa tore through Jamaica and left schools struggling with severe damage, Usain Bolt stepped in to help the communities that
articles.body: Last year, when Hurricane Melissa tore through Jamaica and left schools struggling with severe damage, Usain Bolt stepped in to help the communities that shaped his journey. The sprinting legend joined hands with longtime sponsor Puma to donate J$10 million towards rebuilding two high schools hit hard by the disaster. The contribution brought support to students and teachers facing damaged classrooms and disrupted school life. For Bolt, whose own story began in Jamaican schools and track programmes, the donation also reflects a long-running commitment to giving young people the chance to learn, compete and build a future.Usain Bolt and Puma donated J$10 million to two Jamaican schoolsBolt and Puma each directed J$5 million to St Elizabeth Technical High School, known as STETHS, and William Knibb Memorial High School in Trelawny, where Bolt studied. Both institutions suffered serious damage when Category 5 Hurricane Melissa struck Jamaica in late October 2025.At STETHS in Santa Cruz, the damage included the complete loss of the roof on the Grade 11 block. The building plays a key role for students preparing for Caribbean Secondary Education Certificate exams. Other roofs, teachers' cottages, athletes' dormitories and parts of the perimeter wall also suffered damage. The school's spectator stands were left badly damaged as well.William Knibb Memorial High School reported damage to seven buildings, six of which were severely affected. Several structures lost their roofs, creating an urgent need for repairs before students could return to normal learning conditions.The donations aim to support recovery at both schools, helping restore spaces that matter to students, teachers and the wider communities. Rebuilding classrooms and other facilities is vital not only for everyday lessons but also for students preparing for important examinations and sporting events.Usain Bolt Foundation continues its investment in Jamaican youthThe latest contribution builds on Bolt's work through the Usain Bolt Foundation, which supports education, sport and youth development across Jamaica. The foundation has backed communities in rural parishes including Trelawny, St Elizabeth, St Ann, St James and Clarendon.Earlier in 2025, it provided J$6.1 million in cash and supplies to six rural high schools preparing for the ISSA Boys and Girls' Championships. William Knibb was among the beneficiaries.The foundation has also helped younger children by supplying printers, hygiene stations and learning materials to 21 early-childhood institutions across five parishes. The effort supported more than 1,200 children and their teachers during the COVID-19 pandemic.Bolt's relationship with Puma adds another layer to the relief effort. The brand signed him in 2003, when he was just 16, and the partnership grew alongside his rise to global fame. In 2021, he secured a lifetime deal with Puma, becoming the first track-and-field athlete to receive such an agreement.That long-standing connection now supports a cause beyond athletics. By joining forces to help rebuild damaged schools, Bolt and Puma are directing their influence towards communities facing a difficult recovery. articles.title: Insider Reveals Michigan’s Starting QB vs. Indiana
articles.summary: Michigan is reportedly expected to start Tommy Carr over Bryce Underwood against Indiana after the freshman sparked a comeback win over Penn State.
articles.body:
The Michigan Wolverines appear ready to make a major change at quarterback ahead of Saturday's matchup against No. 6 Indiana. According to new reporting, true freshman Tommy Carr is expected to start against the Hoosiers , replacing Bryce Underwood following Michigan's dramatic comeback victory over Penn State.

The development comes after head coach Kyle Whittingham confirmed Monday that Michigan had selected its starting quarterback but refused to reveal the decision publicly. Now, with multiple reports pointing toward Carr, the Wolverines appear prepared to give the freshman his first collegiate start.

Tommy Carr Expected to Start Against Indiana

According to Pete Nakos' report , Carr is expected to take over as Michigan's starter Saturday. Additional reporting on the quarterback change also indicates the Wolverines are preparing to move forward with Carr while Underwood shifts into a backup role.

Carr earned the opportunity after replacing Underwood at halftime against Penn State with Michigan trailing 3-0. The freshman completed 5 of 7 passes for 47 yards while rushing for 36 yards and a touchdown, helping the Wolverines rally for a 21-18 victory.

As we previously reported , Indiana head coach Curt Cignetti had already indicated that he expected Carr to start Saturday. His assessment now appears consistent with the latest reporting surrounding Michigan's plans.

What Does This Mean for Bryce Underwood?

Underwood struggled against Penn State, completing just 5 of 11 passes for 43 yards while throwing two interceptions. His difficulties protecting the football played a major role in Whittingham's decision to make the halftime switch.

As we previously detailed following Whittingham's comments , the Michigan coaching staff wanted to evaluate both quarterbacks before choosing its starter for Indiana. That decision has apparently gone in Carr's favor, although Whittingham has not publicly confirmed the reported selection.

The freshman will face a significant challenge against an Indiana team looking to rebound from its loss to Ohio State. Carr showed promise against Penn State, but Saturday could provide a much clearer picture of his ability to lead Michigan's offense over an entire game.

For now, Tommy Carr is the reported favorite to start against Indiana, not an officially announced starter. But if the latest reports prove accurate, Michigan will enter one of its biggest games of the season with a new quarterback leading the offense.

articles.title: EFI administrator seeks Rs 25 lakh in damages, serves defamation notice on Hangzhou Asiad gold medallist Chheda
articles.summary: New Delhi: In a bizarre turn of events, Lt Col Sandeep Dewan, member (administration) of the ad hoc committee governing the Equestrian Federation of India
articles.body: New Delhi: In a bizarre turn of events, Lt Col Sandeep Dewan, member (administration) of the ad hoc committee governing the Equestrian Federation of India (EFI), has served a defamation notice on Hangzhou Asian Games gold medallist Hriday Chheda, demanding Rs 25 lakh in damages and an unconditional apology over allegations concerning the handling of the Indian dressage team ahead of and during the recently concluded Aichi-Nagoya multisport continental event.The six-page legal notice, dated October 17 and in possession of TOI, also seeks the withdrawal and deletion of Chheda’s September 8 email to the Indian Olympic Association (IOA) and sports officials, in which the rider alleged that the veterinary report declaring his horse, Dono Di Maggio, unfit was engineered to clear the way for reserve Anush Agarwalla. Chheda accused Dewan of collusion, fraud and concealment, questioning the attempt to jeopardise his participation in the Asian Games.The development raises questions over the priorities of an administrator appointed to restore order in a federation long plagued by governance controversies, internal power struggles and selection disputes. Instead of addressing an athlete’s grievances, the administrator is now seeking damages from one of India’s leading riders for raising concerns about his conduct.For the record, Chheda’s horse, Dono Di Maggio, was subsequently cleared by the Games organisers to compete in Japan. The horse was the best-performing among the Indian riders in Aichi-Nagoya.After being served the notice, Chheda expressed deep anguish over the way he had been treated and wrote a strongly worded email to IOA president P T Usha."The vindictiveness, high-handedness and arrogance is apparent from the attached legal notice. The irony is appalling: an athlete who faced harassment and an attempt to prevent his participation and subsequently demonstrated through his horse’s performances that he was fit to compete, is now facing legal threats from the very person whose conduct he questioned," Chheda wrote to Usha. The email is in possession of TOI."An administration that resorts to legal threats against athletes rather than welcoming scrutiny of its own conduct has no place in sporting governance. Individuals such as Col Dewan must be held accountable for their conduct and questioned on their suitability to hold positions of responsibility in Indian sport," Chheda said."Meanwhile, athletes have received no meaningful support from the Federation and continue to bear the consequences of its failures. The multiple legal disputes concerning the Federation’s functioning, along with the reported suspension by the international governing body, FEI, have further jeopardised athletes’ careers and international participation," he added.Dewan’s notice, however, disputed the allegations, maintaining that the veterinary examination covered all Indian team horses and that the decision on a late replacement rested with the IOA, not with him individually. It stated that the September 8 email falsely accused him of fraud, collusion and concealment, thereby damaging his reputation."The impugned email has gravely harmed my client's reputation as a veteran Army officer, as a sports administrator and as Team Leader. It has exposed him to suspicion and ridicule among the very persons with whom he must work and caused him severe mental distress," Dewan's lawyer, Aroon Menon, stated in the notice issued on his client's behalf."By making and publishing the impugned email, you have committed the offence of defamation under Section 356(1) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, punishable under Section 356(2). My client is the person aggrieved and is entitled to file a complaint under Section 222 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023. Your acts also constitute the civil wrong of libel, for which my client is entitled to sue you for damages, a mandatory injunction directing retraction and a permanent injunction restraining further publication," the lawyer stated."You are therefore called upon within 7 (seven) days of receipt of this notice to: (i) Unconditionally withdraw the impugned email and every imputation in it against my client; (ii) Tender an unconditional written apology to my client, sent by email from hridaychheda98@gmail.com to every recipient of the impugned email, with a copy to the undersigned; (iii) Delete the impugned email and refrain from forwarding, circulating or repeating it or any similar imputation, in any medium, including email, messaging apps, social media and the press; (iv) Pay an amount of Rs 25,00,000 (twenty-five lakh) as compensation to my client for the harm to his reputation and the mental distress caused, and Rs 50,000 (fifty thousand) towards the costs of the present notice," the notice added.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.summary: Recibió asistencia médica sobre el escenario y fue trasladado de urgencia al hospital en ambulancia, pero no sobrevivió
articles.body: El culturista británico Mateusz Chmura murió a los 33 años tras desmayarse durante una competición en Telford (Inglaterra). El incidente ocurrió mientras competía en la división de peso medio de la categoría Classic. El fisioculturista se sintió mal y cayó desplomado sobre el escenario. Tras el colapso recibió asistencia médica sobre el escenario y fue trasladado de urgencia al hospital en ambulancia, pero no sobrevivió. El canal de televisión NTD informó que la intervención de los servicios de emergencia obligó a interrumpir momentáneamente el evento. La competición se reanudó más tarde, tras una reunión con el resto de los deportistas, en un momento en el que los organizadores aún no habían recibido la confirmación del fallecimiento. Mateusz Chmura participaba en las finales nacionales de la Physical Culture Association (PCA), una de las organizaciones de referencia del fisioculturismo. La PCA confirmó finalmente el fallecimiento de Mateusz Chmura a través de sus canales oficiales, sin precisar, hasta el momento, la causa de la muerte. Dos semanas antes del evento en Telford, había logrado el segundo puesto en una eliminatoria de la PCA celebrada en Yorkshire.

articles.summary: Tampa Bay y Milwaukee, los equipos 19 y 28 de la Liga de béisbol según masa salarial, jugarán los partidos por el título. El cuento de Cenicienta aún se mantiene
articles.body: Desde hace unos años no se para de escuchar que el ejemplo del Leicester, ganador de la Premier en la temporada 2015-16, no se volverá a repetir jamás en el fútbol europeo porque, aplicado el efecto Mateo (los ricos serán más ricos), los clubes referencia tienen cada vez más recursos. El transcurrir de los campeonatos en las cinco grandes ligas, así lo avala. Dieciséis equipos se han repartido los títulos (50 en la suma) en la década. Entre seis (Barcelona, Real Madrid, City, PSG, Bayern y Juventus) han acumulado el 72 por ciento de ellos. Casi tres de cada cuatro. La final de la liga estadounidense de béisbol arranca el viernes con dos equipos que no se sitúan en la parte alta de la clasificación salarial de la MLB: Milwaukee Brewers y Tampa Bay Rays, los decimonovenos y los vigésimo octavos de esta lista. Milwaukee, en términos globales el mercado más pequeño de toda la competición, lo hizo batiendo a los Dodgers, una franquicia con más del doble de presupuesto, para construir la final más sorprendente desde 1980. Entonces fue la última vez que llegaron dos equipos a las Series Mundiales sin títulos. Aquí viene la parte incómoda: la televisión. Con dos mercados tan pequeños, se habla del riesgo de arrojar las audiencias más bajas de la historia. Como termómetro, el séptimo partido del año pasado, Dodgers contra Blue Jays, reunió casi 26 millones de espectadores en Fox. Es difícil que Milwaukee y Tampa se acerquen a esa cifra, aunque en las dos ciudades implicadas esto va a ser un acontecimiento sin precedentes. Lo más interesante es que todo ocurre en pleno pulso entre la liga y los jugadores. La MLB lleva tiempo defendiendo la necesidad de un tope salarial y hay un cierre patronal sobre la mesa. El sindicato, en cambio, tiene ahora un argumento a mano: con buenos ojeadores, cantera y gestión, se puede competir por el título. Cada bando leerá estos números a su favor. Los dueños dirán que constituye una excepción, a pesar de que es una competición muy abierta en el que no ha habido dinastías en este siglo. El sindicato esgrimirá que funciona. Con independencia de esto, ver a dos equipos modestos pelear por el título que este año tampoco va a ganar la mayor franquicia del deporte, los New York Yankees, es un motivo de alegría para los últimos románticos.

articles.title: Need to build a larger pool of shooters for consistency: NRAI president Kalikesh Singh Deo
articles.summary: PUNE: The Indian shooters had a decent outing at the recently concluded Asian Games in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan.
articles.body: PUNE: The Indian shooters had a decent outing at the recently concluded Asian Games in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan. The shooters won 15 medals that included 3 gold, 8 silver and four bronze medals and finished second behind China (28 total) in the sports medals tally.Though there was a good haul of medals, the National Rifle Association of India (NRAI) president Kalikesh Singh Deo feels India could have done better at the quadrennial event.“I think the results were decent. In some events, we did pretty well. However, there was one event where we did not meet our expectations, given the strength of the team we had sent,” Kalikesh told TOI.The NRAI president was referring to the air pistol event, where India drew a blank. India didn’t win a single medal from air pistol men and women individual and team categories. Suruchi Phogat and Kamaljeet’s gold in the mixed team event was the only consolation for the Indians.While the women’s team had experienced shooters like Paris Games double medallistManu Bhaker, Esha Singh and Suruchi, the men’s team had an inexperienced squad that included Kamaljeet, Kedarling Balakrishna, and Aakash Bhardwaj.As a lot of new shooters are taking up the 10m air pistol event in the men’s category, it is becoming difficult for players to maintain their spot in the squad. The men’s squad keeps changing from tournaments to tournaments and lacks stability. Kalikesh agreed that always-changing names have made things inconsistent for them.“There have been frequent changes in the composition of the men's air pistol team. Our selection policy is completely objective. We use a rolling average of scores, so we do not exercise discretion in the selection process.However, frequent changes in the team can be a problem because athletes do not get enough time to gain experience. The sports science support we need to provide them also sometimes gets disrupted,” he said.The NRAI chief said that the federation will be looking to find a solution as they face the problem of plenty.“We have to find a way to work with a larger pool of athletes, perhaps even beyond the core team. We had anticipated this issue, not just in air pistol but in some other events as well, where many young shooters have started coming through. In fact, in the year preceding this one, we introduced a policy of sending two teams to international competitions. Alongside the main team, which competed at every World Cup, we sent another team and gave its members ample opportunities. As a result, around 10 to 15 shooters in each discipline have now gained international exposure.”“Having said that, men's air pistol remains an issue we need to address. We are waiting for the World Championships to conclude because we do not want to disturb either the team or the high-performance coaching group at this stage,” he added.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Magnus Carlsen: "Me gustaría estar en el cerebro de Messi"
articles.standfirst: El ajedrecista noruego, número 1 durante 15 años, será la gran atracción de la MOVE Cup de Barcelona
articles.summary: El ajedrecista noruego, número 1 durante 15 años, será la gran atracción de la MOVE Cup de Barcelona
articles.body: La MOVE Cup traerá de nuevo la élite de la ajedrez a Barcelona 37 años después. Entre los participantes en el torneo, que se celebrará del 18 al 20 de enero en la Ciudad Condal, estará el gran maestro noruego Magnus Carlsen. El número uno del mundo se sienta con MARCA para hablar de la MOVE Foundation, de ajedrez y de su futuro. Pregunta. La Fundación MOVE es la organizadora de la competición. ¿Cómo ayudan a la gente a través de ella? Respuesta. Mi manera de ayudar es como jugador. Es muy bonito que el torneo tenga su parte solidaria. Entiendo que uno de los objetivos es ayudar a todas las comunidades que componen el mundo del ajedrez. Siento que el hecho de que exista esta fundación es muy importante para todos los que formamos parte de este deporte. P. Usted que está tan acostumbrado a ganar, que lleva 15 años siendo el mejor en lo suyo, ¿cuándo ha sido la última vez que ha aprendido de una derrota? R. En ajedrez no paras de aprender. Aprendo de las buenas partidas, de las malas, de mi juego, del juego de mis rivales... Saber más no implica directamente que vas a jugar mejor o ser mejor jugador. Muchas veces es difícil utilizar lo que sabes de una manera correcta cada vez que compites. En mi último torneo, perdí un par de partidas y lo recuerdo porque llegó a sorprenderme. En general, yo diría que soy la clase de persona que aprende cada día. P. El ajedrez no es un deporte olímpico. ¿Qué cree que necesitan para que lo sea y si le gustaría? R. Para mí nunca ha sido un objetivo que el ajedrez forme parte de los Juegos y no creo que deba estar, pero lo mismo digo de deportes como el fútbol. Agradezco esta pregunta, de verdad. P. Ahora que las máquinas son imbatibles, ¿qué queda del talento natural de las personas? R. La realidad es que los seres humanos son realmente malos jugando al ajedrez. Yo creo que hubo una época que pensamos que éramos buenos y los ordenadores nos han recordado cuál es nuestro límite. Hay cosas que nunca podremos conseguir y otras que jamás podremos entender. Es un poco triste saber que tenemos unas limitaciones tan grandes con respecto a las máquinas, pero eso hace más interesante la evolución del ajedrez. P. Usted es un gran aficionado a muchos deportes. ¿Si pudiera meterse en el cerebro de un súper atleta a quién elegiría? R. Hay muchos deportistas que podría decir ahora mismo. Por ejemplo, Leo Messi. Porque tengo la sensación de que no piensa demasiado, simplemente juega. Es un talento natural. P. Leí que comentó un día que entre Rafael Nadal y Roger Federer se quedaba con Rafa porque era un trabajador duro e incansable. R. Sí, y es porque yo me reflejo un poco en él. No todo en mí es tan natural ni soy tan rápido como lo pueden ser otros. He visto el documental de Netflix y aún tengo más respeto y admiración por todo lo que hizo en el tenis. Cómo fue capaz de jugar durante tantos años con todos los problemas físicos que fue arrastrando a lo largo de su carrera. Rafa es alguien a quien admiro mucho. P. Hoy en día los dos mejores jugadores del circuito masculino de la ATP son Jannik Sinner y Carlos Alcaraz, considerados como el nuevo ‘Big2’. ¿Con quién se identifica más, el murciano o el italiano? R. Sin duda alguna Alcaraz porque es mucho mejor jugador de golf y a mí me gusta mucho el golf. P. La semana pasada, en el torneo de tenis de categoría Masters 1000 de Shanghái, Alejandro Davidovich firmaba en la cámara tras las victorias con movimientos de ajedrez. Porque suele jugar con su entrenador Pepo Clavet ¿Es importante que eso pase para la promoción de su deporte? R. No sabía que Davidovich lo había hecho y me alegro. Le conozco porque ha ganado a mi compatriota Casper Ruud un par de veces y sé que es un gran jugador. Pero es significativo porque es un ejemplo más de que el ajedrez se está adentrando más y más en la cultura popular de la gente. Lo ves porque muchos atletas juegan. Ojalá que Davidovich siga ganando e introduciendo nuestro juego a los seguidores. P. La MOVE Cup se disputará en Barcelona. ¿Ha bía jugado aquí antes? R. En 2023 estaba en la ciudad de vacaciones y jugué algunas partidas por internet. Pero como torneo será la primera vez y tengo ganas de jugar. La ciudad tiene una auténtica sensibilidad por el ajedrez. En el formato rápido cada partida puede dar un giro en un instante y eso lo hace más emocionante tanto para jugar como para verlo. P. Los otros siete grandes maestros se irán desvelando uno a uno en las próximas semanas y el premio para el vencedor son 300.000 euros. ¿Qué le motiva más de la competición? R. Queremos a los mejores jugando de una manera rápida a la vez que divertida. Para mí el ajedrez es el deporte más interesante del mundo y creo que es bueno para los niños. También me gusta que la bolsa de premios se iguale para la MOVE Foundation, ya que contribuirá al crecimiento del juego y de los jugadores jóvenes.

articles.title: Newcastle United’s Jaissle Transition Will Need Patience & Hard Work
articles.summary: Matthias Jaissle’s high-intensity philosophy faces a stern reality check. As tactical inconsistencies and defensive lapses spark frustration, the Magpies mus...
articles.body:
Newcastle United's transition under Matthias Jaissle was never going to be an overnight success, and recent results have served as a reminder of just how much work remains to be done if the Magpies are to become the side their supporters hope to see.

There is no escaping the disappointment surrounding Newcastle's recent run of form. Defeats against Leeds United and Aston Villa , alongside dropped points against Liverpool and Bournemouth , have raised questions about Jaissle's preferred system, his tactical approach and whether his squad is currently equipped to deliver the football he wants to implement.

However, while the frustration is understandable, it is important to recognise that building a new identity takes time. Newcastle are attempting to establish a different way of playing under a new head coach, and that process requires patience, hard work and a willingness from everyone at the club to embrace the challenges that come with change.

Jaissle arrived with a reputation for aggressive pressing, vertical football and an emphasis on winning possession back quickly. These principles demand exceptional fitness, tactical discipline and complete understanding between players.

When executed properly, such an approach can make Newcastle an incredibly difficult team to face. The intention is to force opponents into mistakes, recover possession in dangerous areas and attack before the opposition has time to reorganise.

The problem is that these methods leave little room for hesitation. If one player fails to press at the correct moment, the opposition can exploit the space left behind. If the midfield is bypassed, Newcastle can suddenly find themselves defending large areas of the pitch with limited protection.

It would be wrong, however, to assume that these problems cannot be corrected. They highlight the areas Jaissle and his coaching staff must address on the training ground.

One of the biggest challenges facing Jaissle is finding the right balance between his footballing philosophy and the strengths of the players available to him.

A preferred formation, such as his favoured 4-2-3-1, can provide a useful starting point, but formations should never become more important than the players operating within them.

Newcastle need to become more difficult to play through, particularly when facing teams capable of exploiting transitions. The midfield must provide sufficient defensive protection while still offering the creativity and forward movement required to create opportunities.

The responsibility does not fall solely on the head coach. The players must take accountability for their performances, improve their decision-making and demonstrate the concentration required to execute the game plan consistently.

Equally, Jaissle must be prepared to adapt. A successful coach is not simply someone who convinces a squad to follow a particular system; it is someone who understands when that system needs adjusting to get the best out of the personnel available.

Nobody should expect supporters to accept poor results without criticism. Performances must improve, and the club must demonstrate that lessons are being learned.

Nevertheless, constantly questioning the direction of travel after every disappointing result risks creating unnecessary instability. If the hierarchy believes Jaissle is the right man to lead Newcastle forward, he must be given the opportunity to develop his ideas, improve the squad and establish a sustainable style of play.

That does not mean providing unconditional backing regardless of results. Progress must be measurable, whether through improved defensive organisation, better midfield control, more consistent performances or a clearer understanding of the team's identity.

The hierarchy must also ensure that Jaissle receives the support he needs in the transfer market, particularly if certain positions are not suited to the demands of his system.

Ultimately, patience alone will not solve Newcastle's problems. It must be accompanied by hard work, honest assessment and visible improvement.

Jaissle needs to show that he can learn from setbacks, make the necessary tactical adjustments and build a team capable of competing against different styles of opposition. The players, meanwhile, must demonstrate that they understand his demands and are prepared to work collectively rather than relying on individual quality to rescue difficult situations.

Newcastle have enough talent within their squad to produce better performances than some of those witnessed recently. The challenge is turning that talent into a cohesive, disciplined and consistent team.

There will be difficult afternoons along the way, particularly while the squad adapts to a new coaching philosophy. What matters is how Newcastle respond to those setbacks and whether the same weaknesses continue to appear without correction.

The verdict is simple: Jaissle's Newcastle transition needs patience, but that patience must be earned through progress.

The Magpies cannot expect to transform into a consistently dominant side overnight. However, with the right coaching, tactical flexibility, commitment from the players and support from the hierarchy, there is no reason why this difficult period cannot become an important stage in the club's development.

Jaissle deserves the opportunity to demonstrate what he can achieve, but the responsibility now rests with him and his players to turn potential into performances and performances into results.

articles.title: Christian Horner reveals new details of controversial 2021 Abu Dhabi GP
articles.summary: Christian Horner has revealed that he deliberately pressured race director Michael Masi to restart the controversial 2021 Abu Dhabi Grand Prix
articles.body:
Christian Horner's memoir, Drive, begins with the contentious 2021 Abu Dhabi Grand Prix - a Formula 1 race that many still find divisive to this day. For the first time, the Briton revealed that he deliberately put pressure on Michael Masi to restart the race after Nicholas Latifi crashed his Williams , causing a safety car.

Red Bull's Max Verstappen and then-Mercedes driver Lewis Hamilton entered the last race of the 2021 season on even points. And in the final laps of the race, Hamilton was ahead, but a freshly pitted Verstappen had new rubber with just five lapped cars between them as they drove the circuit behind the safety car. Overtaking all five cars would be a tough ask for the young Dutchman.

"My heart sank," Horner wrote. "That meant that Max would have to pass all five cars before getting to Lewis, which was impossible in one racing lap.

"I decided to apply some more pressure on race control. 'Come on, Michael, we need to get this race going; why aren't we getting these lapped cars out the way?'"

Masi, in what became a highly controversial move, unlapped only the cars between the pair and restarted the race with just one lap left. This move ultimately gave Verstappen the championship win with him able to easily dispatch Hamilton on his new tyres. Masi was replaced for the 2022 season.

Horner explained on the High Performance Podcast that he only realised that year, once radio messages to the race director began to be broadcast, that Toto Wolff had been speaking directly to Masi.

"Hang on, that's not on? You're putting pressure on the referee here," Horner said. "So I was like to our team manager, 'Get me on the line', because I never spoke to Charlie Whiting in 15 years that he was there."

He insisted Red Bull had done nothing wrong at the end.

"He made the decision, which was within his remit, as per the regulations to be able to do, but it had never been done before, to allow the cars between Max and Lewis to unlap," Horner said. "It wasn't our fault but we're in a position where we've got this one lap to have a crack at it, and if anyone is going to deliver you on a lap like that, it's Max. What happened, happened."

articles.title: Here we go, Fabrizio Romano confirms massive Liverpool transfer is coming
articles.summary: A big Liverpool transfer is on the way according to Fabrizio Romano. It's a busy time for Julian Ward. Just as he is settling in he already has to contend wi...
articles.body:
A big Liverpool transfer is on the way according to Fabrizio Romano.

It's a busy time for Julian Ward. Just as he is settling in he already has to contend with an upcoming transfer window. We may only be in October, but January is just around the corner.

The world of football is fast-paced and doesn't really slow down. It means clubs have to be proactive, and they need to act fast in the market before anyone else catches onto them.

Ward is now being tasked with one of the most fundamental parts of the Liverpool rebuild project. The key essentials have been brought in.

Liverpool have some superstars. What Andoni Iraola needs is a balanced squad, and a team that works together. It's Ward's job to make things work.

Liverpool's biggest priority in the January window

There are still cracks within this Liverpool squad. It's why the start to the season has been far from perfect.

One of the biggest issues within the team is the lack of balance in midfield. Iraola has some absolutely brilliant midfielders. Dominik Szoboszlai has been tremendous for the Reds. Ryan Gravenberch can also be a fantastic midfielder.

But the problem is the two of them simply don't work together. They don't strike the right balanced.

Liverpool have looked far better with Alexis Mac Allister and Trey Nyoni playing, even though the former is someone they are open to selling and the latter is still a youngster.

So, the club's priority will be to bolster their options and bring in a midfielder who would also offer balance.

Fabrizio Romano confirms Liverpool's big transfer is coming

Could they be doing that in the January window?

There were murmurs about Lamine Camara after the end of the summer window, and it is clear that the Reds are planning on a big transfer in 2027 for a midfielder.

Fabrizio Romano has now also confirmed it.

Speaking on his YouTube channel, he revealed Liverpool are intensifying discussions about signing a midfielder.

"So, Liverpool are following Lamine Camara. They have been tracking him for a long time. There have been some calls regarding Alex Scott, and Liverpool have also been tracking Lamine Camara.

"What I can tell you is that Liverpool are planning to do something important in midfield in 2027, adding very good players to that area. So, these are not just backup players. They want players who can be starters or future starters at Liverpool.

"Midfield is an area Liverpool have started considering, not just because of the calls regarding Alex Scott, with Chelsea also interested, and not just because of their appreciation of Lamine Camara. It is also a general consideration. Even in the conversations they are having with the coach, Andoni Iraola, midfield is an area Liverpool want to address in 2027.

"Then, it is a question of whether that happens in January or in the summer. It depends on the opportunity. We know Liverpool's style. Even now, with the new directors, it is not about going out and buying players simply for the sake of buying them or filling a position. Liverpool like to enter the market only when the right opportunity is there, and that will remain the main strategy at Liverpool."

articles.title: Struck by Lightning: 3 Observations as Golden Knights Suffer Rare Blowout Loss
articles.summary: Las Vegas, N.V.– Time and time again, the Vegas Golden Knights have demonstrated a refusal to accept defeat or go quietly into the night. There are certainly...
articles.body:
Las Vegas, N.V.– Time and time again, the Vegas Golden Knights have demonstrated a refusal to accept defeat or go quietly into the night. There are certainly games where they fall behind by multiple goals. Usually, they're able to recover, and the final score is typically close. The thing about the Golden Knights is that they're very rarely on the wrong side of a blowout.

Tonight was one of those rare occurrences.

So far this season, the Golden Knights have played very few teams who are currently in a playoff spot. The Tampa Bay Lightning were just the fourth playoff team the Golden Knights have faced through eleven games, and this matchup could have been a great test of how they stack up against one of the premier teams in the league.

Instead, the Golden Knights fell victim to self-inflicted injury after self-inflicted injury. They entered the second period tied at two apiece, but allowed three goals and never recovered. The third period was entirely noncompetitive, and the Golden Knights ultimately fell 6-2 .

"We had our chances to get ourselves back in the game once it got to five," said Golden Knights captain Mark Stone. "They get that early one in the third, and it's pretty tough to come back from that. We'll stick with it and learn from it… We gotta be better in these games."

"I thought we were a little bit out of our rhythm, a little bit out of our execution, that we had maybe been in for the last nine games. But give [Tampa] credit," said head coach Ryan Craig following the 6-2 loss. "They did a lot to influence that as well."

The final score suggests an extremely lopsided game in which the Lightning thoroughly dominated the Golden Knights, but that wasn't the case. The Golden Knights had no problem generating scoring chances, and they were extremely dangerous in transition.

The problem was that they repeatedly shot themselves in the foot.

"If you turn the puck over against those top guys, they make you pay," said Golden Knights captain Mark Stone following the loss. I think it's definitely unforced errors. When you play against a team like that, you've got to get [the puck] outside the blue line. We had chances on [goals three and four] to get it out, and we didn't."

The Lightning scored four unassisted goals tonight, which means that most of their offense came directly off of Golden Knights' turnovers.

"We didn't help ourselves. I think that would be the easiest way to put it," said head coach Ryan Craig. "I mean, they scored four unassisted goals tonight. We probably didn't put ourselves in good positions to get out of areas, and then gave them chances to attack."

"It probably goes back to puck management a little bit, right? Both teams are good at checking as well, and I think some of the situations we put ourselves in didn't help," continued Craig. "We probably just got a little bit cute at times, which led to being up and down a little bit. But if you don't manage the puck, that's what it's gonna feel like."

Prior to tonight, Ivan Barbashev was in a rut. He didn't have any problem generating offense; heading into tonight's game, Barbashev had seven points and was tied for fourth on the team in scoring. The problem was that his offense wasn't translating into goals. All seven of his points were assists, and for a scoring forward playing on a line with Jack Eichel and Mark Stone, that statistic had to be weighing on him.

That's no longer an issue. Barbashev scored the first goal tonight for the Golden Knights, which tied the game at one apiece.

Barbashev can be a bit of a streaky scorer, and in the past, it only takes one goal to open the floodgates. Look for him to get on the board again on this upcoming two-game road trip to St. Louis and Columbus.

Even after a blowout loss, the Golden Knights aren't too concerned with their level of play.

"It's game eleven; I don't think there are measuring stick games in game eleven," said Golden Knights' captain Mark Stone following the 6-2 loss. "We're still trying to build our game going forward. We're playing 84 games this year, and we're trying to build our game to go on a long playoff run. It starts at game one; we're in game eleven. We still like where we're at, as far as our record, but we want to get better."

Because they're only eleven games into the season, the Golden Knights can use tonight's loss as a learning opportunity. They won't hang onto the loss any longer than necessary. They'll sit with it, and then move on and learn from their mistakes.

"When you play good teams, you're not gonna come back from [being down] four in the third," said Stone. "We have to correct your mistakes and build off some of the good stuff we did, because there was some good stuff. We had lots of chances. How did we create those chances… And what bad plays did we make to give them chances? That's what we try to learn from."

articles.title: Cleverley apologises for 'unacceptable' Argyle loss
articles.summary: Plymouth Argyle manager Tom Cleverley apologises for his side's "unacceptable" performance in their 3-0 League One loss at Stevenage.
articles.body:
Plymouth Argyle manager Tom Cleverley has apologised for his side's "unacceptable" performance in their 3-0 loss at Stevenage on Tuesday.

The Pilgrims lost back-to-back games in League One for the first time since early February as they slipped to fifth in the table, having sat top last week.

"I absolutely hold my hands up and apologise for that performance this evening because it's unacceptable," Cleverley told BBC Radio Devon.

"When you represent a big club, you get a lot of pats on the back when it's going well and these players have built up some credit over the last 11 months.

"But that can diminish very quickly with performances like that and we need to not take that support for granted - you need to earn that support, you need to earn those pats on the back and we certainly didn't do that tonight."

Plymouth conceded twice in an eight-minute spell midway through the first half before Stevenage scored a third late in the second period.

The loss came after a 2-0 defeat at home by Huddersfield Town which Cleverley described as "humbling".

"The bare minimum I have to coach, demand, pick a team to be able to do is compete and the last two games we've not at all," he said.

"If you don't compete, if you don't win duels, if you don't land on seconds [second balls], if you don't run and fight then you're going to find it difficult to score goals and difficult to keep it out the back of your net and that is what tonight looked like.

"Two centre forwards who were well managed by two centre-halves at one end and two centre forwards who caused mayhem at the other end, and in between that not much better either.

"So a lot of questions from the last two games and it's my job to provide the answers and real clarity and direction come Thursday to make sure we know exactly how to go get a result on Saturday, and I'm pretty sure top of the priorities will be picking a team that is going to fight and compete."

articles.title: ‘Feeling uncomfortable’ – Andoni Iraola explains why he subbed off one Liverpool player last night
articles.summary: Andoni Iraola has downplayed fears of another injury to his Liverpool squad in explaining one of his substitutions in the 4-3 win over Villarreal on Tuesday...
articles.body:
Andoni Iraola has downplayed fears of another injury to his Liverpool squad in explaining one of his substitutions in the 4-3 win over Villarreal on Tuesday night.

Despite equalising for the Reds on the stroke of half-time, Ronald Araujo was withdrawn at the interval and replaced by Florian Wirtz, with Ryan Gravenberch moved from a number 10 role to right-back.

The tactical reshuffle paid dividends as the home side ultimately prevailed at Anfield, and the head coach explained that the substitution was purely by choice and not forced upon him by any physical issue for the Uruguay defender.

Iraola explains his decision to sub off Araujo

In his post-match press conference, Iraola was asked whether Araujo is OK after being withdrawn at half-time.

The Basque replied (via liverpoolfc.com ): "Yes. In the first half, it has cost us until the 2-0 to balance the game a little bit.

"I think in possession we've got much better positions from Trey [Nyoni] and Alexis [Mac Allister] to control it a little better, but without the ball they were overloading us in the middle with three holding midfielders and [Alberto] Moleiro, who basically is another midfielder coming inside. Ronald was feeling uncomfortable following all the way.

"At the end we thought that a player like Ryan Gravenberch could do both jobs – defensively following inside, even I think he's good enough outside to sustain the one-v-ones, and also offensively could be a better help if you want for Rio [Ngumoha], attacking down the right side."

Want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust

The half-time withdrawl of Araujo may have seemed surprising at first, but the performance of Gravenberch in an unfamiliar right-back role and the improved balance within the team meant that Iraola's decision was vindicated.

Although the Uruguayan is a highly popular figure at Anfield, in truth he didn't have his best night prior to his equaliser, looking unusually uncomfortable up against Moleiro and the roving Sergi Cardona and lacking quality with his deliveries into the penalty area.

The Netherlands international also struggled in the number 10 role but looked much more at home after switching to right-back, being comfortable on the ball and showing plenty of defensive awareness.

The decision to bring on Wirtz also had the desired effect as the German enjoyed another strong performance , capped by his first goal of the season with what ultimately proved to be the winner for Liverpool.

Full credit to Iraola for being proactive enough to make what seemed a risky substitution and trusting his judgement, with the change working out for the best and Araujo thankfully not suffering any injury complaints.

articles.title: Chivas squeak by Necaxa to grab lackluster victory
articles.summary: Chivas defeated Necaxa by a 1-0 score in a match that failed to bring the excitement.
articles.body:
Chivas finally got back to their winning way by defeating Necaxa by a 1-0 score. It was their first victory in more than a month in Liga MX but their performance was far from what was expected and they were lucky to get the victory. Chivas will now travel north to face Monterrey in a stadium where they had some good results. Necaxa will host last placed FC Juarez.

The 1st half started with Chivas giving a start to Jordan Carrillo while Necaxa surprised by not going out from the start with Julian Carranza. Roberto Alvarado got off a left footed shot from outside the area that went just wide. Alvarado would get the ball and made a run into the area where he got off a left footed shot but Necaxa's goalkeeper, Javier Orantes, would make a good save of the close range shot. Leonel Calderon got off a left footed shot from outside the area that went well wide. Richard Ledezma got off a right footed shot from outside the area that went just wide. The halftime whistle blew and the fans in the stadium booed after such a terrible display of football from both teams.

The 2nd half started with Chivas subbing out Jordan Carrillo and Leonel Calderon for Santiago Sandoval and Hugo Camberos. From outside the area, Emilio Rodriguez got off a left footed shot that went well wide. After getting the ball in the area, Ricardo Marin got off a right footed shot that went wide. A right footed shot from Camberos forced a save from Orantes although the play was ruled to be offside. Necaxa subbed out Juan Valencia and Emilio Rodriguez for Julian Caranza and Owen Gonzalez. Chivas subbed out Diego Campillo and Richard Ledezma for Bryan Alonso Gonzalez and Kevin Castañeda. Off a corner kick, Agustin Oliveros rose to get off a close range header that was brilliantly saved by Chivas's goalkeeper Raul Rangel, who then cleared the ball off his feet before Carranza could get to the rebound. A cross form Sandoval turned into a shot that Orantes easily saved. Mauro Zaleta got off a left footed shot that forced another good save from Rangel. Chivas subbed out Efrain Alvarez for Jesus Hernandez. A shot from outside the area by Castañeda would go so close that it moved the net and most in the stadium thought he had scored. After getting past a defender, Alvarado got off a good cross that Agustin Oliveros would deflect past Orantes to score an awful own goal that gave Chivas the 1-0 lead. It was a terrible play from Oliveros as Orantes would have easily handled the ball had Oliveros not tried to clear it. Necaxa subbed out Lorenzo Faravelli for Joshua Palacios. A give and go ended with Carranza getting the ball in the area but his right footed shot went well wide. Gonzalez got off right footed shot wide open in the area but his volley was terrible and it easily fell to Rangel. Necaxa subbed out Diego Ochoa for Missael Pedroza. Off a free kick, the ball was headed just out of reach of Emilio Martinez, who would have had a tap in chance had he gotten to it. Javier Ruiz got off a great right footed shot from way outside the area but Rangel made a wonderful save. Chivas held on to the win although their fan still disapproved of such a mediocre display by their team.

Chivas got their first win since September 13 against Pumas. While Chivas got the victory, it seemed an unfair result as Necaxa had done a good enough job that a tie would have been more deserved. Chivas only scored because of an own goal and created few opportunities. Chivas had a hero on goalkeeper Rangel as they held on for dear life against a Necaxa side that is now in 17th place. Chivas will travel north to face Monterrey in Estadio BBVA, a stadium where they have had a lot of success to the surprise of many. Necaxa will travel home where they will host the last placed FC Juarez.

articles.title: 76ers’ Joel Embiid issues strong defensive declaration in locker room after beating Knicks
articles.summary: Joel Embiid is very clearly not the player he once was due to all the injury problems he’s gone through over the past few years. But the Philadelphia 76ers m...
articles.body:
Joel Embiid is very clearly not the player he once was due to all the injury problems he's gone through over the past few years. But the Philadelphia 76ers may not need him to be his MVP-level self anyway, at least in the early goings of the season. On Tuesday night, the 76ers spoiled the New York Knicks' ring night and handed them a 106-101 loss even with Embiid having a subpar offensive outing .

Embiid finished with just 13 points on 4-of-15 shooting from the field, and he mostly lived from the perimeter. Nearly half of his shots came from beyond the arc (he went 2-of-7) and he deferred to the 76ers' other stars — with Tyrese Maxey leading the way with 28 points on the night.

However, Embiid made a concerted effort to anchor the 76ers' defense. He helped Philly limit New York to just 37.2% shooting from the field, and there were times where he made it impossible for the Knicks to score in the paint. He had two steals and three blocks on the night, too. After the game, the 76ers star declared that he wants to get back to being at his best on the defensive end.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

"Embiid had a declaration to make in the locker room after this one. He said, 'I'm going to get back to being an all-defensive team player,'" Dave McMenamin of ESPN said on SportsCenter, via Oh No He Didn't on X.

According to McMenamin, Embiid also suggested that the 76ers put LeBron James on Karl-Anthony Towns , which then bottled up some of New York's pick-and-pop actions — forcing their other players, who were struggling with their shot, to get the ball.

With James and Jaylen Brown now on the roster, the 76ers have so much talent on offense that they can afford Embiid to take it easier on that end of the floor. If Embiid returns to being a major force on defense, Philly well and truly may have what it takes to mount a challenge for the Larry O'Brien trophy.

articles.title: Pistons’ Cade Cunningham is loving the ‘blessing’ that makes his life easy on the court
articles.summary: The consensus on the Detroit Pistons heading into the 2026-27 season was down, as they lost solid veteran contributor Tobias Harris in free agency. Moreover,...
articles.body:
The consensus on the Detroit Pistons heading into the 2026-27 season was down, as they lost solid veteran contributor Tobias Harris in free agency. Moreover, they did not make many meaningful additions to the roster this past offseason, and they had to deal with the drawn-out restricted free agency of Jalen Duren. But Cade Cunningham showed on opening night that he's the man as he led Detroit to a come-from-behind 121-113 victory over the Boston Celtics.

The Pistons fell down by 13 at the halftime interval, and the Celtics pushed their lead to as many as 22 points. However, Detroit buckled down on the defensive end just in time for their shots to start falling. While Cunningham finished with just 22 points on the night, he received plenty of help from veteran Duncan Robinson, who had 21 points of his own after drilling five threes. Javonte Green also stepped up off the bench, nailing five triples of his own.

Cunningham credited the Pistons' shooters for making their shots when it mattered, which made life so much easier for him and the rest of the team.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

"It's a blessing. It makes my life easy. It makes [Jalen Duren] and [Ausar Thompson]'s life easier. We just got to keep getting our camaraderie, our synergy a little bit better. But that'll come as the season goes," Cunningham told Robbie Hummel of NBC Sports in his postgame interview.

Isaiah Joe, Kevin Huerter, and Daniss Jenkins combined to make four triples as well, and their mere presence on the court demands respect from the opposition's perimeter defenders. This then gave Cunningham, Duren, and Thompson so much space to operate.

But at the end of the day, the Pistons will make a living off of their elite defense . They posted the league's second-best defense last season, and there's no reason to believe that they'll get worse at that end of the floor. However, if they combine that with some improved outside shooting, perhaps another 60-win season could be in the cards.

articles.title: Opposition Lowdown: 12th-Placed Leyton Orient
articles.summary: Reading return to the SCL this Wednesday for a midweek game under the lights against Leyton Orient. Join us as we take a closer look at the opposition.
articles.body:
Leyton Orient finished 20th in League One last season, only one place and three points clear of the relegation places. This season marks their fourth straight season in the third tier, following their promotion from League Two in 2023, when they finished as champions.

They have had a relatively strong start to the current season, sitting 12th in the league, four places and one point behind Reading in eighth.

Their recent from has been mixed, having seen two wins, one draw and two losses in their last five league matches. They come into this Wednesday's game off the back of a 2-0 home win against Blackpool after goals from Will Forrester and Dane Scarlett.

The two sides shared the spoils last season, with Reading winning 2-1 at home last September before Orient claimed a 3-1 home win back in January, via a hat-trick from former Reading loanee Dom Ballard.

Richie Wellens: Wellens was appointed Orient manager in March 2022, taking over from Kenny Jackett, who was sacked after nine months in charge.

Wellens was a midfielder during his playing career, having come through the Manchester United academy. He appeared for the likes of Blackpool, Leicester City and Doncaster Rovers over the course of an 18-year professional career.

He began his coaching stint in 2017, starting out at Oldham Athletic, where he was then appointed manager. His next managerial role came at Swindon Town, where he secured promotion to League One after the season was cut short due to Covid-19.

A four-month spell at Salford City followed in 2020, after which he joined former club Doncaster in 2021, where he lasted six months.

Wellens secured promotion in his first full season at Leyton Orient, winning the League Two title and the manager-of-the-season award. He has since guided the Os to 11th-, sixth- and 20th-placed finishes in League One.

The 46-year-old likes his teams to play attacking football and, having strong links to Manchester United, sees Sir Alex Ferguson as one of his greatest inspirations.

It was a busy summer in East London, with Orient signing 16 players – 11 coming in permanently and five joining on loan.

The Os paid fees for goalkeeper Nathan Baxter (Watford), defender Fin Stevens (St Pauli), midfielder Armando Dobra (Chesterfield) and strikers Jaze Kabia (Grimsby Town) and Dane Scarlett (Tottenham Hotspur).

They also utilised the free market, picking up defender Joseph Olowu, midfielders Isaac Hayden, Alex Gilbert and Cristian Pascaluta, winger Tony Springett and forward Tariq Al Sadi.

Their loans were goalkeeper Oliver Dovin (Coventry City), defenders Somto Boniface (Ipswich Town) and Alfie Gilchrist (West Bromwich Albion), winger Yusuf Akhamrich (Tottenham) and Nick Oyekunle (Southampton).

Lineup : Baxter, Olowu, Forrester, Gilchrist, Stevens, Gilbert, Hayden, Morris, Akhamrich, Connolly, Scarlett

6. Will Forrester: Defender Forrester joined Orient this January, signing from Bolton Wanderers for an undisclosed fee.

He started his career in the youth setup at Stoke City and made his professional debut while at the Potters in 2021. Forrester made a further three appearances for Stoke before moving to Port Vale on a permanent deal in 2022, where he stayed for one season.

A move to Bolton Wanderers followed a year later, where Forrester made 53 appearances over the course of two-and-a-half seasons. Since joining Orient, the 25-year-old has made 28 appearances for the club, scoring two goals, with one of those coming over the weekend.

Forrester is a ball-playing centre-back with strong leadership skills, who was named club captain for the second half of last season.

9. Jaze Kabia: Forward Kabia signed for Leyton Orient over the summer, joining from Grimsby for a club-record fee.

He started his career in his homeland of Ireland, making his professional debut at Cobh Ramblers in 2018, before also spending time at Shelbourne. A move to Scotland followed in 2021 when Kabia moved to Livingston, before returning to Ireland with Cork City in 2023.

A short spell back in Scotland with Clyde followed, before he gained his first taste of English football with non-league Truro City in 2024. The following summer, Kabia joined Grimsby Town in League Two, where he finished as the club's top scorer on 23 goals.

The 26-year-old has five Orient goals to his name since joining this summer. Kabia is a striker who is a good finisher, while also being able to play out wide.

articles.title: Tyrese Maxey keeps it real about Kentavious Caldwell-Pope after 76ers win vs. Knicks
articles.summary: NEW YORK — After the Philadelphia 76ers’ longest-tenured player Joel Embiid told Tyrese Maxey he felt something different from within during a 106-100 win ag...
articles.body:
NEW YORK — After the Philadelphia 76ers ' longest-tenured player Joel Embiid told Tyrese Maxey he felt something different from within during a 106-100 win against the New York Knicks on Opening Night, the All-Star guard understood what he meant, pointing to the championship experience LeBron James, Jaylen Brown, and Kentavious Caldwell-Pope bring to the table. After his 76ers debut, James said Maxey's speed impressed him most .

While most are quick to point to the 76ers' All-Star additions of James and Brown over the summer as critical, Maxey reminded a reporter of Caldwell-Pope, whom Maxey says is a key voice and veteran with championship experience in the team's locker room.

"We got 3. KCP came, too. That's underrated because his talk is exceptional. And what he's done for this group. He played well tonight. Not just his play, but his talk, his growth as a leader. We're gonna need it," Maxey said. "We're gonna need it throughout the year. And Bron and JB; we know what they do. They brought championship pedigree. We're going to lean on those guys to lead us."

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

76ers veteran Kentavious Caldwell-Pope won a championship alongside LeBron James with the Los Angeles Lakers in 2020. For 76ers All-Star Tyrese Maxey, all three bring championship pedigree that matters just as much for Philadelphia this season. For a team that added nine new players with one goal in mind, Maxey isn't overlooking the importance of listening to players who have won it all.

76ers' Jaylen Brown, who led the Celtics to a title in 2024, was named Boston's Finals MVP. After spoiling the Knicks' championship-banner-raising night at Madison Square Garden, the 76ers will host the Cleveland Cavs in their home opener on Wednesday.

Caldwell-Pope finished with 13 points on 5-for-10 shooting, including a pair of threes in the fourth quarter, four rebounds, one assist, and one block. Maxey finished with a game-high 28 points, five assists, four rebounds, three steals, and three blocks in Tuesday's win.

After capitulating inside 40 overs in their first innings for 140 against Mumbai on Day One, Himachal's batters finally showed some grit and gumption on Day Three of their Elite Group D Ranji Trophy match against Mumbai in Bilaspur, Himachal Pradesh. Opener Innesh Mahajan (37, 91b, 5x4), skipper Pukhraj Mann (34*, 94b, 5x4) and wicketkeeper-batter Vaibhav Kalta (14*, 70b, 3x4) all did well to stonewall Mumbai and delay the visitors' charge towards an innings win. At stumps, Himachal were 144/3 in 56 overs, still trailing by 244 runs. Earlier, Mumbai wicketkeeper-batter Akash Anand slammed a century (117*, 239b, 14x4), while Sarfaraz Khan made 154 (228b, 19x4) as Mumbai declared at 528/8.

Sai Kishore hat-trick helps TN beat Uttarakhand by an innings

At Chepauk, Tamil Nadu captain and left-arm spinner Sai Kishore took a hat-trick as his team crushed Uttarakhand by an innings and 66 runs inside three days. In the 43rd over, Sai Kishore bowled Lakshya Raichandani on the fourth ball, had Saurabh Rawat caught in the slips off the fifth, and then had Aditya Rawat caught behind as TN bowled out Uttarakhand for 113.

Vidarbha beat J&K by three wickets in thriller

In Srinagar, Vidarbha overcame Jammu & Kashmir by three wickets in a low-scoring thriller. Chasing a target of 79 in the final innings, Vidarbha collapsed to 26/6 and then 55/7 before Harsh Dubey (22*) and Nachiket Bhute (13*) took them home.

A brave century by middle-order batter Manan Hingrajia (108*, 274b, 12x4, 1x6), a half-century by Joymeet Patel (72, 119b, 9x4) and a useful contribution from skipper Chintan Gaja (41*, 105b, 3x4) helped Gujarat, who resumed at 98/2, reply strongly to Delhi's 648/6. At stumps on Day Three, Gujarat were 363/5, still trailing by 285 runs. articles.title: Spurs struggle to defend 3-point line in season-opening loss to Thunder
articles.summary: Victor Wembanyama pointed to a failure to make the "extra effort" out on the perimeter, a factor in OKC's Jared McCain hitting 6 of 8 from deep.
articles.body:
Oklahoma City guard Jared McCain's basketball career is more precious to him after knee and thumb injuries plagued his first two seasons.

"I love playing basketball," he said. "This is something I've loved since I was younger. When I was injured, it was just the worst time ever. So being able to be out there playing any minutes (Thunder coach) Mark (Daigneault) gives me, I'm happy and I'm grateful for it. And being able to play with these guys, my teammates, it's really fun out there.

"I just have fun when I play. It's good vibes."

McCain created plenty of "good vibes" for Oklahoma City on Tuesday night, when he connected on 6 of 8 from 3-point range on his way to scoring 20 points in 22 minutes off the bench in the Thunder's 116-104 season-opening victory over the Spurs.

The Spurs finished last season ranked eighth in the league in opponents' 3-point efficiency, holding foes to 35.2% from beyond the arc.

But there wasn't a carryover from that strong effort into the 2026-27 opener at the Frost Bank Center.

Sparked by McCain, Oklahoma City hit 45.2% from long range (14 of 31).

"Just not running them off the line, not closing to touch, especially early," Stephon Castle said when asked what went wrong for the Spurs out on the perimeter. "That's how they got up on us kind of early."

The Thunder led 65-44 at halftime after leading by as many as 26 points in the first half. McCain went into the break with 11 points on the strength of 3 of 4 from long range.

As a team, Oklahoma City hit 10 of 14 from 3-point territory in the first half (71.4%).

Spurs All-Star center Victor Wembanyama said several factors led to the sub-par defensive showing.

"I think there were some times where we were really, really good and we (didn't) finish the possession," the 2026 Defensive Player of the Year said. "Sometimes there (were) moments when we gave them two offensive boards on the same position, or we play great defense, get the ball off of their hot guys, and (then) we barely do a closeout or we do a bad closeout or we miscommunicate.

"It's like they were playing the right way. I'm sure they were having fun tonight. They were making the extra pass and we weren't making the extra effort."
